item.title: Daily News Briefing - 2026-11-26
item.description:
Daily News Briefing - 2026-11-26
Topics covered: - Dario Amodei, Anthropic's chief executive, has rejected claims that his company wants humanity to "surrender human free will" to AI, calling the idea "absurd." TechCrunch reports that in a long post on X he wrote that "turning over governance to AI is a bad idea." He suggested drawing a line at recursive self-improvement, meaning AI that improves itself without human help, and wrote that "we may want limits on this process." The pushback follows remarks from rivals - Nvidia's governance troubles now carry a price - On trade, the United States trade representative has proposed new tariffs on fourteen partners, including the European Union, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea - In privacy news, forty-two state attorneys general are trying to stop bankrupt Character.AI from auctioning chat histories from more than twenty-one million American accounts, over two million of them belonging to minors - Finally, the Federal Communications Commission has conditionally authorised SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites designed as orbital data centers - Next week, Huang faces Congress just as the Character.AI auction tests whether bankruptcy can override a privacy promise
